title: Onboarding Concierge: network posture scorer and prioritized remediation lanes for private/VPC requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
We receive frequent private/VPC/on-prem onboarding requests where the primary friction is heterogenous customer network posture (proxy, egress restrictions, MTLS, air-gapped registries). Current intake is manual, inconsistent, and often misses early network blockers until runbook time which increases time-to-value and eng churn.

Goal:
Create a lightweight 'Onboarding Concierge' that synthesizes a customer's network posture into a concise score and recommended remediation lanes, so PMs and onboarding engineers can: (1) prioritize requests objectively, (2) route customers to fast-lane vs runway lanes, and (3) auto-generate the next-step checklist for the customer. This ticket scopes the PM work and acceptance criteria for an initial MVP.

Scope (MVP):
- A customer-facing questionnaire (web form + intake template) that maps to ~12 binary/choice probes (e.g., egress allowed to S3, outbound ports 443/80, private registry access, KMS/HSM on-prem, proxy auth type, MTLS support).
- A scoring rubric that converts answers into a 0-100 'Network Posture Score' and a 3-tier priority recommendation: Fast-lane, Standard onboarding, Engineering runway.
- Automated remediation lane templates (email + task list) for the top 6 common blockers (proxy auth, blocked egress, docker registry reachability, TLS inspection, restricted DNS, custom NAT).
- An internal PM dashboard row summarizing score, estimated engineering days (heuristic), and suggested SLA bucket.

Out-of-scope for MVP: full automation of probes, agent-based network scans, legal/contract changes, in-depth security assessments.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simplicity vs accuracy: Use questionnaire heuristics instead of active probes to keep MVP low-effort and customer-friendly. We accept increased false positives early as long as remediation lanes are clear.
- Human touch vs self-serve: Build templates for onboarding engineers to review rather than fully automated decisions; this preserves a safety net for complex accounts.
- Scope creep risk: Keep initial remediation list limited to the most frequent blockers we observed in the last 12 months.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Customers may mis-report environment; mitigation: include 'confidence' checkboxes and request network logs for low-confidence profiles.
- Legal/security edge cases: escalate when KMS/HSM or air-gapped enforcement is selected.
- Engineering capacity: prototype scripting for the dashboard with one full-time eng for two sprints.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A completed intake template that converts to a Network Posture Score for 100 sample historical requests with scores matching manual raters within +/-15 points.
2) Three remediation lane templates (proxy, egress, registry) created and validated by Solutions Eng with copy and task checklist.
3) PM dashboard row prototype that shows score, suggested SLA bucket, and heuristic estimated eng-days.
4) Internal playbook documented in Confluence and an intake email template ready for CS/AM.
5) Stakeholder review completed (Eng, Solutions, Security), with a go/no-go decision recorded.
proposed_solution:
- Intake: Build a short web form and a Google Docs intake template for PM/CS teams. Map each field to a weight in the posture scorer.
- Scoring: Simple weighted sum of probes -> normalize to 0-100. Define buckets: 80-100 (Fast-lane), 50-80 (Standard), 0-50 (Engineering runway).
- Remediation lanes: Author 6 ready-made checklists with step-by-step actions, sample commands, and commonly required customer artifacts (e.g., pcap, traceroute).
- Dashboard: Add a single row in the existing Private Deploy dashboard (Console-ops) showing score + suggested SLA + notes.
- Handoff: Generate a templated email and Jira/Linear outbound ticket for Engineering when 'Engineering runway' is recommended.
rollout_plan:
Week 0: Stakeholder review and intake questionnaire draft.
Week 1: Build form + scoring spreadsheet; author 3 remediation templates.
Week 2: Internal validation with 20 historical requests; iterate.
Week 3: Dashboard prototype and PM/Eng review.
Week 4: Pilot with two new customers and collect feedback.
Post-pilot: Measure time-to-activation and adjust weights.
